title: [B1 • Band 5.0] Bài 303: Sunken Archives: Deep-Sea Archaeology
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 303 (LEVEL B1 • BAND 5.0)

Sunken Archives: The Ethics of Deep-Sea Archaeology

Paragraph 1. For centuries, the deep ocean floor acted like a locked vault, keeping thousands of ancient shipwrecks safe beneath miles of water. Over the past twenty years, however, improved sound sonar and deep-diving robots have opened up the deep seabed. In her book Treasures of the Abyss, maritime archaeologist Dr. Elena Gomez examines the fierce conflict between commercial treasure hunters and scientific researchers.

Paragraph 2. To private salvage companies funded by investors, historic wrecks are simply underwater banks. Firms spend millions sending robotic submarines down to collect gold, silver coins, and valuable porcelain, selling them at auctions to earn big profits. Dr. Gomez argues that this destroys real history. In scientific archaeology, an object's exact physical context—its precise spot next to the hull and cargo—provides nearly ninety percent of its historical value. When mechanical claws scoop coins hastily, that irreplaceable data vanishes forever.

Paragraph 3. On the other hand, commercial firms argue that without private money, deep shipwrecks would stay untouched forever. State museums and university teams face tight public budgets and cannot afford tens of millions of dollars to rent research ships. Companies suggest sharing projects: selling 'duplicate' objects to cover costs while donating unique pieces to museums. Gomez rejects this idea, noting that calling historic artifacts 'duplicates' is merely a business trick to justify looting.

Paragraph 4. Legal gaps make the problem even worse. In open international waters far beyond national borders, local heritage laws have zero legal power. Although the 2001 UNESCO treaty stated that underwater artifacts should never be sold commercially, major sea powers like the United States and the United Kingdom refused to accept it. Without strict global rules, our shared underwater history risks being quietly emptied.

groups.title: Questions 6–10
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer? Write YES, NO, or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 2: "...selling them at auctions to earn big profits."

q6.text: Private salvage companies donate every silver coin they find to public museums.

steps: Đoạn 2: Họ bán đấu giá để kiếm lời cho cổ đông, không tặng hết cho bảo tàng.

q7.text: Dr. Elena Gomez previously worked for a commercial salvage firm before writing her book.

steps: Đoạn 1: Bài chỉ giới thiệu bà là nhà khảo cổ học hàng hải và tác giả cuốn sách.

q8.text: Recording an object's exact underwater spot provides most of its historical value.

steps: Đoạn 2: Vị trí chính xác mang lại tới gần 90% giá trị lịch sử.

q9.text: Public museums often lack sufficient funding to hire expensive research vessels.

steps: Đoạn 3: Ngân sách công eo hẹp khiến bảo tàng không đủ chi trả hàng chục triệu đô la.

q10.text: National heritage laws protect shipwrecks even in open international oceans.

steps: Đoạn 4: Ngoài vùng đặc quyền kinh tế quốc gia, luật di sản nội địa không có hiệu lực pháp lý.
